gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 9?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 9 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Current forecasts from major models place Munich's August 11 maximum near 30–31 °C, slightly above the long-term mid-August average of ~23–25 °C.** This positioning explains why those two outcomes dominate the market at 36.5 % and 44.5 %.

A warm-air advection pattern under high pressure has followed the early-August heat wave (daily highs reached 31–36 °C early in the month before cooling to 24 °C by August 6). Latest ensemble runs from the German Weather Service (DWD) and ECMWF keep southerly flow and limited cloud cover through the 11th, supporting afternoon temperatures in the low-30s °C range. Minor disagreements among models on exact cloud timing and boundary-layer mixing create the tight spread between 30 °C and 31 °C; a slightly earlier marine influence or extra low-level stratus could cap the peak at 30 °C, while clearer skies would favor 31 °C or marginally higher.

Traders are weighting the consensus of the most recent high-resolution runs and the established warm anomaly rather than climatology alone. Updated model cycles and any DWD short-range guidance issued in the next 24–48 hours remain the key catalysts that could shift the narrow 30–31 °C balance before resolution.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 10 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the London City Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/gb/london/EGLC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus shows near parity between 26°C and 27°C as the expected maximum in London on August 10, reflecting tight ensemble spread in short-range models. Primary drivers include the strength of high pressure over southern England, surface heating under mostly clear skies, and light variable winds that limit mixing with cooler air from the North Sea. Urban heat island effects in central London can add 1–2°C locally compared with rural sites, while any increase in afternoon cloud cover or a weak frontal boundary would cap the peak nearer 26°C. Official Met Office and ECMWF guidance currently brackets these values, with resolution depending on the verified daily maximum from approved stations.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office guidance and short-range ensemble models point to a peak of 24–26°C across London on August 11 under building high pressure that favors subsidence, clear or broken skies, and light winds conducive to daytime heating. This setup follows a summer already running 1.8–2.4°C above the 1991–2020 baseline, yet the immediate steering pattern introduces modest uncertainty in boundary-layer mixing and any thin residual cloud or weak warm-air advection from the south. Official forecasts emphasize predominantly dry conditions, with the highest reading expected at the London City Airport or Heathrow reference station; small differences in insolation or timing of any frontal moisture could shift the single maximum by 1–2°C. Model updates over the next 24–48 hours remain the dominant driver of trader positioning around the current 24–25°C cluster.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 9 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the LaGuardia Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/us/ny/new-york-city/KLGA.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: National Weather Service forecasts and ensemble model consensus for New York City on August 9, 2026, point to a daily maximum near 90–91°F, supported by warm advection, mostly sunny skies, light winds, and a heat advisory reflecting above-normal August conditions. This strong scientific alignment from official monitoring underpins the near-certain market-implied odds for that bin. Sea-breeze development along the coast or unexpected afternoon convection could cap readings slightly lower, while any delay in cloud cover or stronger southerly flow might push isolated spots briefly higher, though model spread remains narrow around the central forecast.

Minor disagreements among models on exact cloud timing and boundary-layer mixing create the tight spread between 30 °C and 31 °C; a slightly earlier marine influence or extra low-level stratus could cap the peak at 30 °C, while clearer skies would favor 31 °C or marginally higher.

Updated model cycles and any DWD short-range guidance issued in the next 24–48 hours remain the key catalysts that could shift the narrow 30–31 °C balance before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official Met Office guidance for London on August 11 projects a daytime maximum of 26°C under building high pressure, with sunny intervals, light winds, and minimal cloud cover favoring radiative heating. This aligns with the broader summer pattern already running 1.8–2.4°C above the long-term average. Ensemble model spreads introduce modest uncertainty around boundary-layer mixing and any residual moisture or thin high cloud, which could trim the peak by 1°C. Trader positioning—favoring 24–25°C outcomes at combined ~81% implied probability—reflects these variables and recent cooler daily readings amid a post-heatwave transition, while short-range forecast updates remain the key catalyst likely to shift market-implied odds.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 11 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency project a maximum temperature of 30°C in Tokyo on August 11 under mostly cloudy skies with rain developing later, which limits solar heating and caps peaks below typical clear-sky values. This outlook aligns with broader summer 2026 guidance for above-normal temperatures across Japan driven by a strong Pacific High, though daily variability from cloud cover and precipitation probability around 50% in afternoon hours tempers extremes. Historical August baselines average 31–32°C, yet recent model consensus supports 29–30°C as the most probable range given the expected steering patterns and moisture influx. Upcoming JMA updates on the morning of the 11th will refine resolution thresholds tied to official station observations.

**Official short-term forecasts position 28–30°C as the most likely range for Tokyo’s August 11 high.** The Japan Meteorological Agency’s 3-day outlook issued August 10 forecasts a high of 30°C under cloudy skies with rain developing later in the day, alongside a 50–60% chance of precipitation after midday. This aligns closely with the market’s leading outcomes (29°C at 38.5%, 30°C at 22.5%, 28°C at 21.5%).

**Persistent summer heat and seasonal context reinforce the consensus.** August is Japan’s hottest month, with Tokyo’s normal daily maximum near 31.6°C. Broader seasonal outlooks from JMA indicate above-normal temperatures nationwide through summer 2026, driven by a strengthened Pacific High after the Baiu rainy season. Recent weeks have featured frequent 30–35°C days, but the immediate forecast for August 11 incorporates moderating cloud cover and rainfall that can suppress peak heating.

**Traders appear to weight slight downward adjustments from the 30°C point forecast.** Incoming rain and increased cloudiness introduce uncertainty in maximum temperature, as evaporative cooling and reduced solar insolation can trim 1–2°C from potential peaks. Historical analogs for similar late-summer setups with afternoon rain support a distribution centered on 28–30°C rather than higher values. The low probabilities assigned to 31°C+ (under 8% combined) reflect this near-term cooling influence ahead of resolution. Updated model runs or JMA briefings on August 10–11 could further refine these implied probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent high-pressure building over southern England, combined with abundant sunshine and light winds, forms the main driver positioning 25°C (48.5% implied probability) as the leading outcome for London's August 11 maximum at official stations such as London City Airport. Ensemble forecasts from the Met Office and European models show modest spread in boundary-layer mixing and any residual cloud, keeping 24°C (38.5%) close behind while limiting upside risk to 26°C (9.5%). The current summer baseline already runs 1.8–2.4°C above the long-term August average, amplifying insolation effects, though dry air and minimal warm advection cap further gains. Short-range model runs over the next 24 hours remain the key catalyst for any shifts in trader positioning.

Updated NWS briefings and afternoon model runs remain the key near-term catalysts.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest National Weather Service and AccuWeather model guidance for August 10, 2026, positions New York City’s daily maximum in the upper 80s to low 90s, aligning with trader consensus favoring 90–91 °F. Persistent high pressure and southwesterly flow are supporting above-normal temperatures, consistent with the Climate Prediction Center’s August outlook for warmer-than-average conditions across the Northeast. Central Park’s 1991–2020 normal high of 83 °F provides context, while urban heat-island effects and dew-point values near 70 °F can add 2–4 °F to observed readings. Afternoon model updates or unexpected cloud cover and sea-breeze shifts remain the main variables that could nudge the official high reported by LaGuardia or Central Park stations into the 88–89 °F or 92–93 °F bins.

The Japan Meteorological Agency’s latest three-day guidance highlights cloudy skies with occasional scattered showers and 50–60% precipitation probability, which limits solar insolation and caps daytime heating below the seasonal normal of roughly 31–32°C. Ensemble model consensus and recent runs show limited diurnal temperature rise under these conditions, producing the tight clustering of market-implied odds around 27°C (26.5%) and 28°C (32.5%). 

Slight variations in shower timing, cloud thickness, or localized clearing could shift the official JMA station reading by 1°C in either direction, explaining the narrow spread versus lower-probability outcomes at 29°C or below 27°C. Longer-range signals, including a strengthened Pacific High supporting elevated seasonal temperatures, remain secondary to these short-term synoptic details two days before the observation window. Updated JMA briefings and model runs will provide the next key data points for refining probabilities.

Updated model runs overnight and early-morning satellite data will likely tighten consensus ahead of resolution.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 10 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent high-pressure ridging over Central Europe has driven warm southerly advection into Bavaria, with German Weather Service (DWD) and ECMWF model consensus projecting a daily maximum of 34 °C at Munich Airport station on August 10. Real-time observations through midday align closely with this guidance, showing temperatures climbing toward but not clearly exceeding that threshold amid light winds and limited cloud cover. The 95 % market-implied probability on 34 °C reflects traders’ confidence in the official measurement window and historical model accuracy for this synoptic setup. A modest shift in steering flow or unexpected convective cooling could still cap the peak at 33 °C, while stronger insolation or delayed sea-breeze effects represent the narrow path to 35 °C.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from major meteorological models indicate a daytime maximum near 30–31°C for Munich on August 11, driven by warm advection under weak high pressure and partly cloudy conditions that limit full solar heating. Ensemble spreads of 1–2°C arise mainly from afternoon cloud development and variable boundary-layer mixing, which can suppress or enhance peak readings by a degree depending on timing. Historical August climatology for the region shows typical highs around 24–26°C, so current guidance reflects above-average warmth from a persistent southerly flow. Traders weigh these model differences against resolution on official station data, with the tight 30°C–31°C split reflecting uncertainty in exact peak timing and any late-day cooling.

eventMetadata.context_description: A warm, humid air mass across the Northeast, supported by ensemble model consensus from NOAA and regional guidance, positions New York City for a daily maximum in the 88–91°F range on August 10. This aligns with the market’s heaviest weighting on the 90–91°F bin (48%) and 88–89°F bin (30.5%), as limited cloud cover and light steering winds favor strong daytime heating above the long-term August average of 83°F. Recent model runs have narrowed uncertainty around this interval rather than signaling major shifts, with only modest probability (16%) assigned to 92–93°F under scenarios of slightly stronger insolation or delayed mixing. Higher bins remain low-probability outcomes given the absence of extreme heat advection or blocking patterns in current forecasts. Traders monitor afternoon observations and any final NWS adjustments, which could refine implied odds before official Central Park resolution.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office guidance for London on August 10, 2026, centers on a daytime maximum near 27°C amid building high pressure, sunny intervals, and light northerly winds, which has anchored trader consensus around 26°C as the leading outcome. Above-average conditions relative to the August climatological baseline of roughly 22–23°C reflect stable anticyclonic patterns suppressing cloud cover and allowing greater insolation. Minor downward revisions in short-range model runs have slightly elevated the 25°C probability while keeping 27°C and higher outcomes in low single digits, consistent with ensemble spread and observational trends through the morning. Upcoming afternoon verification data from official stations will refine these market-implied odds.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest ensemble runs from the UK Met Office and ECMWF show London's maximum temperature on August 12 clustering tightly around 30–31°C, driving the near-even market split between those two outcomes. Subtle differences in how models handle a strengthening high-pressure ridge, boundary-layer mixing, and urban heat-island effects create the remaining spread, with a modest warm bias relative to the 1991–2020 August average. As the event nears, each new 00Z or 12Z model cycle can shift probabilities by a few percentage points; traders are therefore watching the next high-resolution updates for any consistent drift above or below the current 30–31°C window.

Above-average warmth stems from southerly flow and strong insolation under mostly clear to partly cloudy skies, while small differences in predicted cloud timing or boundary-layer mixing could shift the daily maximum by 1 °C. Historical August maxima in Munich average roughly 23–25 °C, so the current outlook represents a notable positive anomaly; resolution rests on the official station reading, with any late forecast update from DWD likely to move the tight 30 °C versus 31 °C spread.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency position 29°C as the most likely daily high for Tokyo on August 11, aligning with the market’s leading 38% implied probability.** Issued on August 10, the JMA outlook calls for cloudy skies with rain developing later, yielding a maximum of 29°C and minimum of 22°C. This cloud cover and precipitation reduce incoming solar radiation, limiting afternoon heating compared with clearer summer days.

Persistent seasonal warmth from a strengthened Pacific High keeps baseline temperatures elevated for mid-August, yet the approaching weather system introduces enough moisture and reduced insolation to cap the peak near 28–30°C. Historical August climatology in Tokyo shows typical highs of 30–33°C under full sun, but recent model consensus and the explicit JMA guidance explain why probabilities cluster tightly around 28–30°C while outcomes above 31°C or below 27°C receive far less market weight. Traders appear to be weighting the authoritative short-term forecast most heavily, with any morning updates on August 11 likely to refine these odds further.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official short-term forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency position Tokyo’s August 11 high near 29°C under initially partly cloudy conditions that give way to increasing cloud cover and a 50–60% chance of afternoon rain, a key moderating factor that can suppress peak solar heating and differentiate the closely matched 28–30°C market outcomes. Seasonal context reinforces this range, as August remains Japan’s warmest month with a normal daily maximum of 31.6°C, yet recent model guidance incorporates above-normal Pacific High influence tempered by localized moisture and reduced insolation. Traders weigh the balance between persistent summer warmth and these diurnal suppression mechanisms, with uncertainty in exact cloud timing and rainfall intensity keeping implied probabilities distributed across the 28–30°C band rather than concentrating on higher or lower thresholds. Updated JMA guidance and ensemble model runs will refine resolution criteria ahead of market close.

Updated JMA short-range forecasts and observational adjustments from the central Tokyo station will provide the next resolution-relevant signals ahead of the August 12 close.
